key_insight: In linear-elastic homogenization, the equilibrium Ising Hamiltonian is two-local, but homogenized stress is a one-local observable evaluable from the same computational-basis measurements.
engineering_relevance: The formulation extracts effective RVE stress for macroscale constitutive response without reconstructing the microscopic displacement field or changing measurement basis.
method: Encode the reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Differentiate the strain-dependent Hamiltonian via Hellmann–Feynman to obtain stress observables containing only identity and single-qubit Pauli-Z terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE but provides no quantitative accuracy or performance metrics.
watch_item: Encoding discretization and VQE approximation may affect stress accuracy; computational advantage is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
